check_command_rule.command_absent_at_head: any command_path absent at the head being verified -> FAIL_CLOSED CHECK_COMMAND_ABSENT_AT_HEAD (CHECK_COMMAND_PATHS_PRESENT_AT_HEAD); the state of older heads such as StegVerse-Labs/.github#3225 (e6ba9601) and #3226 (f82c0324) for schema-validate, unit-tests and mutation-negative-suite
check_command_rule.command_undeclared: offline_command UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED (or anything that is neither a non-empty argv nor a verifier built-in) -> FAIL_CLOSED CHECK_COMMAND_UNDECLARED (CHECK_HAS_OFFLINE_COMMAND); the only acceptable receipt for such a check is the verifier's FAIL_CLOSED CHECK_COMMAND_UNDECLARED with the six fields (generic; no check in this row is in that state)
check_command_rule.evaluator: resident-runtime/sv_work_items.py::check_command, check_outcome_matches (pure over supplied paths and outputs)
check_command_rule.pass_criteria_live_in_the_row: A head never declares its own pass criteria; it binds them through required_checks_ref.blob_sha. The NWI-S1 verifier runs offline_command from the repo root at the exact head with no network (argv; placeholders only from argument_bindings) and compares the outcome with expected (exit_code; stdout_json_subset keys must equal; stderr_last_line must equal).
check_command_rule.verifier_builtin: offline_command {verifier_builtin, verifier_ref, predicate} (all non-empty strings; verifier_builtin = the check id) names a command built into the NWI-S1 verifier at verifier_ref, not a script in this repo. command_paths is [] and CHECK_COMMAND_ABSENT_AT_HEAD does not apply; expected is the verifier's own outcome ({disposition: ALLOW}). sv_work_items.verifier_builtin / command_declared / check_command.

check_derived_issue_rule.not_ledgered: FAIL_CLOSED SOURCE_RECEIPT_NOT_LEDGERED: before the org writer appends the receipt the issue cannot be NATIVE
check_derived_issue_rule.opened_by_session: derivation:sv_work_items.derive_issue_from_check_receipt (the id never depends on who runs it; no lane owns minting)
check_derived_issue_rule.resolution_class_rule: a check-derived issue is resolved only through merge admission of an SV_CHANGE that cites it in resolves (class B, as in the P1 FAIL_CLOSED register)
check_derived_issue_rule.source_receipt_ref: the org-ledger ref of the organization-transition receipt whose repo receipt carries the check receipt as $.evidence: refs/stegverse/organization-ledger@<commit>:receipts/<receipt_sha256 hex>.json @ receipt_sha256
check_derived_issue_rule.surface: the check's command surface (sv_work_items.check_command_surface: argv[1], the unittest module file, or this row file when the command is undeclared or a verifier built-in)

statements: (1) Lane B's NWI-S1 verifier (SV-LLM/.github#46) runs each declared check offline at the exact head and emits a six-field, head-bound receipt (schemas/sv-check-receipt.v1.schema.json) carrying the supplied hb_epoch.
(2) That receipt becomes a LEDGER_RECEIPT only through the org-ledger writer transition (StegVerse-Labs/.github#3255, the writer-only workflow) under the shared lock.
(3) The check ids in this row are exactly the ids the verifier emits; no other minter exists. A receipt for any other check id is refused (CHECK_ID_UNDECLARED).

argument_bindings.{base_commit}: supplied by the verifier: the 40-hex commit the head is verified against, already present in the local clone (no fetch); never inferred. An unresolvable base makes the script itself FAIL_CLOSED REGISTRY_GENERATION_UNREADABLE (exit 1).

offline_command.predicate: the readback receipt sealed by Labs#3266 at base_ref.ledger_head carries an observed epoch (else FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED); the SV_CHANGE's hb_epoch that is absent, null, "", "null" or UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED is FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (checked before 726248a5); any other value must pass 726248a5 validation and equal the sealed epoch by integer value (else DENY HB_EPOCH_MISMATCH)

726248a5.kind: sha256 of a function source segment (not a git object)
726248a5.precedence: UNKNOWN precedence (contract invariant, orchestrator 2026-10-18T15:59Z, narrowed 16:03Z): before 726248a5 is applied, a supplied hb_epoch that is the epoch source (an SV_CHANGE record's hb_epoch; an absent field reads as null) and is JSON null, "", "null" or the literal UNKNOWN_NOT_AUTHENTICALLY_OBSERVED is FAIL_CLOSED HB_EPOCH_SOURCE_UNOBSERVED (UNKNOWN is FAIL_CLOSED, never DENY). An optional cross-check that is left out (sv_work_items.HB_EPOCH_NOT_CROSS_CHECKED) is not a failure: the sealed epoch stands. Here the verifier deliberately diverges from kernel.py::supplied_epoch_failure, which alone would return HB_EPOCH_NOT_SUPPLIED for null and HB_EPOCH_INVALID (malformed, DENY here) for "", "null" and the sentinel. The pin is unchanged: it still describes the rule applied to every other supplied value and to the sealed slot.
726248a5.segment_rule: sha256 of the text from 'def supplied_epoch_failure' to the next top-level 'def', trailing whitespace stripped (SV-LLM/.github#46 tests/test_s1_hop_head_verifier.py; Labs#3266 hashes the ast source segment, same digest)
